html:
A dance and music born in the late 1800s in the poor port districts of Buenos Aires and Montevideo, on the River Plate.

It grew out of the crowded tenements of the migrant boom, mixing the rhythms of Afro-Argentines and Afro-Uruguayans, the Cuban habanera, the local milonga and the songs of Italian and Spanish newcomers. Its signature instrument became the bandoneón, a kind of concertina brought from Germany. Early tango was danced in bars, dance halls and brothels, and polite society looked down on it.

Around 1912 and 1913 tango became a craze in Paris and London. Once Europe approved, the Argentine elite embraced it too. In the 1920s and 1930s the singer Carlos Gardel made the tango song famous worldwide through records and films. Later, Astor Piazzolla mixed it with jazz and classical music.

In 2009 UNESCO listed tango as part of the cultural heritage of Argentina and Uruguay. Like samba in Brazil, it rose from the margins to become a symbol of the nation.
sum: A dance and music born in the late 1800s in the poor port districts of Buenos Aires and Montevideo, on the River Plate.
